defects.source_says: EO 12163 section 1-905 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12163.txt): 'The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979.'; the order is signed September 29, 1979 (44 FR 56673). The claim's own judgment_reason says 'First end 1979-10-01' and its research_rationale records the first end as October 1, 1979. An order signed in 1979 cannot end a clause in 1976; the date is wrong and internally inconsistent with the claim's reasons.

EO 12163 section 1-905 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12163.txt): 'The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979.'; the order is signed September 29, 1979 (44 FR 56673). The whole-order end must equal the latest clause first end, which the sources put at 1979-10-01; the research_rationale states October 1, 1979.

reasoning: The legal theory is sound and source-supported: EO 11417 only inserts words into section 305 of EO 10973; EO 12163 section 1-903(a)(1) revokes EO 10973 'as amended', section 1-505 replaces the Development Loan Committee membership with a list that omits the inserted office, and section 1-905 makes the order effective October 1, 1979. No earlier end appears in the order's own terms, the held amenders, or the Cruden search, and the savings analysis is accurate. But the claim's first_end.date and whole_order_end.date both read 1976-10-01, three years before EO 12163 was signed, contradicting section 1-905 and the claim's own judgment_reason and research_rationale (1979-10-01). A wrong end date in the dated fields is a disqualifying defect, so the claim is rejected despite correct reasoning. Corrected to 1979-10-01 with no other change, the claim would appear supportable; the 1973 statutory reorganization of the Committee (section 204 to section 122(e)) is disclosed as not claimed and no held source shows it ended section 305 earlier.
